description: §8.10 Tier 2 loop hoisting × §19.8.3 (RUNTIME, sqlEngine:"real"): a HANDLED keyed read in a `for` body, `const row = ?{…WHERE id = ${it.id}}.get() !{ _ :> not }`. The loop is still rewritten to one pre-fetch + a per-iteration Map lookup, and the handled read keeps its meaning: id 7 → the row, id 8 → `not` (no row is not a failure), and when the pre-fetch fails to run (`gone` is declared but never created) every iteration takes the arm's `not`. Pre-S455 (found by the S455 consumer enumeration of g-impl1-handled-sql-lowering-defects-s455) the hoist rewrite did not see the guarded statement, the pre-fetch ran but the loop body kept the query lowered with no server boundary — `null /* client cannot evaluate */` — so EVERY row read `not` even on success ("none,none"), and a failing pre-fetch threw past the handler.
rationale: §8.10: "A for-loop whose body contains a single keyed `?{}` read SHALL be rewritten to a single `WHERE IN (...)` pre-fetch plus per-iteration `Map` lookup." §8.10.3: "The rewritten loop is observationally equivalent to the un-rewritten loop". §19.8.3: a handled query's success value is the unhandled one's; only a query that fails to run reaches the arms.
